notes.definition: A reversible reaction is a reaction in which the products can react to produce the original reactants. It is shown by the symbol ⇌, for example A + B ⇌ C + D.
explanation: Most reactions you meet, such as burning a fuel, go in one direction only: the reactants change into products and the products cannot easily be turned back. In some chemical reactions, however, the products can react together to produce the original reactants again. These are called reversible reactions. They are represented with the symbol ⇌ instead of a single arrow, so a general reversible reaction is written A + B ⇌ C + D.

The reaction from left to right (A + B forming C + D) is called the forward reaction. The reaction from right to left (C + D forming A + B) is called the reverse reaction, or backward reaction. Both reactions are part of the same reversible reaction. In the reverse reaction the substances on the right-hand side act as the reactants and the substances on the left-hand side are the products.

The direction of a reversible reaction can be changed by changing the conditions. The most common condition to change is temperature. For example, when ammonium chloride is heated it breaks down (decomposes) into ammonia and hydrogen chloride. When the gases are cooled they react together to reform ammonium chloride:
ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride
NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + HCl(g)

You can see this in a simple experiment. White ammonium chloride is heated at the bottom of a test tube. The solid seems to disappear from the bottom because it decomposes into two colourless gases. The gases rise up the tube to the cooler part near the top, where they react together again and a white solid of ammonium chloride forms on the inside of the tube. This is a chemical change, not just the solid turning into a gas, because new substances (ammonia and hydrogen chloride) are made and then react again.

Another example is heating blue hydrated copper sulfate. It loses water and turns into white anhydrous copper sulfate. Adding water to the white powder turns it blue again. In an open container, a reversible reaction may seem to go only one way because a product (for example a gas) escapes and cannot react back. Mass is conserved in both directions: the total mass of products formed equals the mass of reactant used up.
keyFacts: In a reversible reaction the products can react to produce the original reactants.
The symbol ⇌ shows that a reaction is reversible.
A + B ⇌ C + D: left to right is the forward reaction, right to left is the reverse reaction.
The direction of a reversible reaction can be changed by changing the conditions, such as temperature.
Heating ammonium chloride: ammonium chloride → ammonia + hydrogen chloride.
Cooling the gases: ammonia + hydrogen chloride → ammonium chloride (white solid reforms).
Blue hydrated copper sulfate ⇌ white anhydrous copper sulfate + water.
If a gaseous product escapes from an open container, it cannot react back to form the reactants.
Mass is conserved in both the forward and the reverse reactions.

keyTerms.definition: A reaction in which the products can react to produce the original reactants.
The symbol used in an equation to show that a reaction is reversible.
The reaction from left to right in the equation, in which the reactants form the products.
The reaction from right to left in the equation, in which the products react to reform the original reactants (also called the backward reaction).
Breaking down a substance into simpler substances by heating it, for example ammonium chloride into ammonia and hydrogen chloride.
A white solid, NH₄Cl, which decomposes on heating into ammonia and hydrogen chloride; the gases reform the solid on cooling.

equations.name: General reversible reaction
equations.symbols: forward: A + B → C + D; reverse: C + D → A + B

workedExamples.title: Identifying forward and reverse reactions
workedExamples.question: Hydrogen and iodine react in a reversible reaction: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g). Write the equations for the forward and reverse reactions and name the reactant(s) in each.
steps: The forward reaction goes from left to right: H₂ + I₂ → 2HI. The reactants are hydrogen and iodine.
The reverse reaction goes from right to left: 2HI → H₂ + I₂. The reactant is hydrogen iodide.
In the reverse reaction, the substance on the right of the ⇌ becomes the reactant.
workedExamples.answer: Forward: H₂ + I₂ → 2HI (reactants hydrogen and iodine). Reverse: 2HI → H₂ + I₂ (reactant hydrogen iodide).

workedExamples.title: Using conservation of mass
workedExamples.question: A sealed tube contains 5.35 g of ammonium chloride. It is heated until all of the solid has decomposed. The mass of ammonia formed is 1.70 g. Calculate the mass of hydrogen chloride formed.
steps: Mass is conserved: mass of ammonium chloride = mass of ammonia + mass of hydrogen chloride.

workedExamples.title: Explaining an observation
workedExamples.question: A student heats ammonium chloride in a test tube. After a few minutes there is less white solid at the bottom of the tube and a white solid has appeared near the top. Explain these observations.
steps: At the hot bottom of the tube, ammonium chloride decomposes into ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases (forward reaction), so the solid at the bottom gets less.
The gases rise to the cooler top of the tube.
At the lower temperature, ammonia and hydrogen chloride react together (reverse reaction) to reform solid ammonium chloride.
workedExamples.answer: The reaction is reversible: heating drives the forward reaction at the bottom, and cooling at the top drives the reverse reaction, reforming the white solid.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think ammonium chloride is just subliming (turning from solid to gas) when it is heated.
misconceptions.right: In fact it decomposes into two new substances, ammonia and hydrogen chloride, which then react to reform ammonium chloride on cooling. It is a chemical change.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a reversible reaction is any change that can be undone, such as melting ice.
misconceptions.right: In fact the term describes chemical reactions in which the products react to reform the original reactants. Melting is a physical change, not a reversible reaction.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the forward and reverse reactions need different chemicals to happen.
misconceptions.right: In fact the reverse reaction uses the products of the forward reaction as its reactants. Only the conditions (such as temperature) are changed.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think that if a reaction does not reverse in an open beaker, it cannot be reversible.
misconceptions.right: In fact a gaseous product may simply escape, so it is no longer there to react back. The reaction is still reversible.

realWorld: Anhydrous copper sulfate is used as a test for water: it turns from white to blue when water is added, and the blue crystals turn white again when heated.
Cobalt chloride paper is blue when dry and turns pink with water, a reversible colour change used to test for water and in some humidity indicators.
The Haber process makes ammonia for fertilisers using the reversible reaction nitrogen + hydrogen ⇌ ammonia, so not all of the reactants are converted in one pass.
examTips: Always use the ⇌ symbol (two half arrows) when writing equations for reversible reactions; a single arrow loses the mark.
Learn the ammonium chloride example word for word: ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride, with heating for the forward reaction and cooling for the reverse.
When asked what is observed, describe what you would see (white solid disappears at the bottom, white solid forms near the top), not just the chemistry.
If asked how to change the direction of a reversible reaction, say 'change the conditions' and give a specific example, such as heating or cooling.
summary: In a reversible reaction the products can react to form the original reactants.
The symbol ⇌ shows a reaction is reversible.
Left to right is the forward reaction; right to left is the reverse reaction.
Changing the conditions can change the direction of the reaction.
Ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride: heat forwards, cool backwards.
Mass is conserved in both directions.

flashcards.front: In A + B ⇌ C + D, what is the reverse reaction?
flashcards.back: C + D → A + B (right to left).

flashcards.front: How can the direction of a reversible reaction be changed?
flashcards.back: By changing the conditions, for example heating or cooling.

flashcards.front: Word equation for heating ammonium chloride
Symbol equation for the ammonium chloride reaction
What happens to ammonia and hydrogen chloride when they are cooled?
flashcards.back: They react together to reform white solid ammonium chloride.

flashcards.front: Why does white solid appear near the top of a tube of heated ammonium chloride?
flashcards.back: The gases rise to the cooler part of the tube, where the reverse reaction reforms ammonium chloride.

flashcards.front: What happens to blue hydrated copper sulfate when heated?
flashcards.back: It loses water and becomes white anhydrous copper sulfate; adding water turns it blue again.

flashcards.front: Why might a reversible reaction seem to go one way only in an open container?

questions.question: Which symbol is used in an equation to show that a reaction is reversible?
markScheme: 1 mark: ⇌
questions.explanation: The ⇌ symbol (two half arrows pointing in opposite directions) shows that the reaction can go both forwards and backwards. A single arrow → shows a reaction that goes one way only.

questions.question: Which statement describes a reversible reaction?
markScheme: 1 mark: products can react to produce the original reactants
questions.explanation: This is the AQA definition. Melting is a physical change, and catalysts and energy changes do not define whether a reaction is reversible.
options: A reaction that only happens when a catalyst is added
A reaction that gives out energy and then takes it in
A reaction in which the products can react to produce the original reactants
A reaction in which a solid changes into a liquid

questions.question: Ammonium chloride is heated. Which two substances are formed?
markScheme: 1 mark: ammonia and hydrogen chloride
questions.explanation: NH₄Cl → NH₃ + HCl. The ammonium chloride splits into ammonia and hydrogen chloride. Chlorine and hydrogen are elements and are not formed.

questions.question: Ammonium chloride is heated at the bottom of a test tube. What is seen near the cool top of the tube?
markScheme: 1 mark: a white solid
questions.explanation: The ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases react together at the cooler top of the tube, reforming white solid ammonium chloride.

questions.question: For the reaction A + B ⇌ C + D, which substances are the reactants in the reverse reaction?
markScheme: 1 mark: C and D
questions.explanation: The reverse reaction goes from right to left: C + D → A + B. So in the reverse reaction C and D are the reactants.

questions.question: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases are mixed. Which change in conditions makes them react to form solid ammonium chloride?
markScheme: 1 mark: cooling the gases
questions.explanation: The forward reaction (decomposition) happens on heating, so the reverse reaction (forming ammonium chloride) happens on cooling.

questions.question: Which statement about the direction of a reversible reaction is correct?
markScheme: 1 mark: it can be changed by changing the conditions
questions.explanation: The AQA specification states that the direction of reversible reactions can be changed by changing the conditions, for example the temperature.
options: It can be changed by changing the conditions
It can never be changed once the reaction starts
It only depends on the mass of reactant used
It only goes forwards if a catalyst is used

questions.question: Blue hydrated copper sulfate is heated strongly. What colour is the solid left?
markScheme: 1 mark: white
questions.explanation: Heating removes the water, leaving white anhydrous copper sulfate. Adding water turns it blue again, showing the reaction is reversible. Black copper oxide only forms on much stronger heating and is not part of this reaction.

questions.question: Which of these reactions is reversible under normal laboratory conditions?
markScheme: 1 mark: ammonium chloride decomposing when heated
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride reforms when its decomposition products are cooled. Combustion reactions and metal plus acid reactions cannot easily be reversed by changing conditions.

questions.question: A student says: 'When ammonium chloride is heated it just sublimes, like iodine.' Which piece of evidence best shows that a chemical reaction happens instead?
markScheme: 1 mark: two different gases with different properties from the solid are produced
questions.explanation: Sublimation would give gaseous ammonium chloride, the same substance. Forming two new substances (ammonia and hydrogen chloride) shows that bonds are broken and a chemical reaction takes place. The other observations would also be seen with sublimation.
options: The solid at the bottom of the tube disappears
A white solid forms at the top of the tube
Two different gases with different properties from the solid are produced

questions.question: Ammonium chloride is heated in an open evaporating basin instead of a test tube. Very little white solid reforms. What is the best explanation?
markScheme: 1 mark: gases escape, so cannot react to reform ammonium chloride
questions.explanation: The reaction is still reversible, but the products are gases. In an open basin they spread out into the room before they can cool and react together, so little solid reforms.
options: The reaction is not reversible in a basin
The ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases escape into the air, so they cannot react to reform ammonium chloride
The ammonium chloride melts instead of decomposing
Heating in a basin uses a lower temperature

questions.question:
A sealed tube contains 2.14 g of ammonium chloride. It is heated until all of the ammonium chloride has decomposed.
What is the total mass of ammonia and hydrogen chloride formed?
markScheme: 1 mark: 2.14 g
questions.explanation: Mass is conserved in a chemical reaction. No atoms are lost or gained, so the total mass of the products equals the mass of the ammonium chloride: 2.14 g.

questions.question:
Heating 5.35 g of ammonium chloride in a sealed tube produces 1.70 g of ammonia and some hydrogen chloride.
Calculate the mass of hydrogen chloride produced.
markScheme: 1 mark: mass of HCl = 5.35 − 1.70
1 mark: 3.65 g
questions.explanation: Mass of reactant = mass of products, so mass of hydrogen chloride = 5.35 − 1.70 = 3.65 g. Check: 1.70 + 3.65 = 5.35 g.

questions.question:
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of ammonium chloride, NH₄Cl.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): N = 14, H = 1, Cl = 35.5
markScheme: 1 mark: 53.5
questions.explanation: Mr = 14 + 4 + 35.5 = 53.5. A common error is to count only one hydrogen atom, giving 50.5.

questions.question:
A student heats 5.00 g of ammonium chloride in a test tube. After cooling, 4.28 g of white solid is collected from the top of the tube.
Calculate the percentage of the ammonium chloride that reformed. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.explanation: Percentage = 4.28 ÷ 5.00 × 100 = 85.6%. Less than 100% reforms because some gas escapes from the open tube or some solid is left on the glass elsewhere.

questions.question:
Ammonium chloride decomposes: NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + HCl(g)
Calculate the maximum mass of ammonia that can be formed by completely decomposing 26.75 g of ammonium chloride.
Relative formula masses (Mr): NH₄Cl = 53.5, NH₃ = 17
markScheme: 1 mark: moles NH₄Cl = 26.75 ÷ 53.5 = 0.500 mol
1 mark: moles NH₃ = 0.500 mol (1:1 ratio)
1 mark: mass NH₃ = 0.500 × 17 = 8.5 g
questions.explanation: Moles of NH₄Cl = 26.75 ÷ 53.5 = 0.5. The equation shows 1 NH₄Cl gives 1 NH₃, so 0.5 mol NH₃ forms. Mass = 0.5 × 17 = 8.5 g. Check: HCl would be 0.5 × 36.5 = 18.25 g, and 8.5 + 18.25 = 26.75 g.

questions.question: State what the symbol ⇌ in a chemical equation tells you.
markScheme: 1 mark: the reaction is reversible (can go forwards and backwards)
questions.explanation: The ⇌ symbol means the reaction is reversible: the products can react to reform the reactants.
acceptedAnswers: the reaction can go in both directions
products can react to form the reactants

questions.question: Write a word equation for the reversible reaction that happens when ammonium chloride is heated. Use the correct symbol.
markScheme: 1 mark: ammonium chloride on the left, ammonia + hydrogen chloride on the right
1 mark: ⇌ symbol used
questions.explanation: The equation is ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride. Using a single arrow would not show that the reaction is reversible.

questions.question: Give one example of a reversible reaction.
markScheme: 1 mark: any correct reversible reaction, for example ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride
questions.explanation: Common examples are the decomposition of ammonium chloride, dehydration of hydrated copper sulfate and the Haber process reaction.
acceptedAnswers: hydrated copper sulfate ⇌ anhydrous copper sulfate + water

questions.question: State how the direction of a reversible reaction can be changed.
markScheme: 1 mark: by changing the conditions (for example, temperature)
questions.explanation: Reversible reactions can be made to go in the forward or reverse direction by changing the conditions, such as heating or cooling.

questions.question: Describe what a student would observe when solid ammonium chloride is heated gently at the bottom of a test tube.
markScheme: 1 mark: white solid at the bottom gets less / disappears
1 mark: white solid appears near the (cooler) top of the tube
questions.explanation: Observations are what you see. The solid at the bottom decomposes into colourless gases, and the white solid reforms higher up where the tube is cooler.
acceptedAnswers: white solid disappears from the bottom
white solid forms near the top of the tube
white solid forms on the cooler part of the tube

questions.question:
When ammonium chloride is heated in a test tube, a white solid forms near the top of the tube.
Explain why.
markScheme: 1 mark: ammonia and hydrogen chloride (gases) rise to the cooler part of the tube
1 mark: they react (reverse reaction) to reform ammonium chloride
questions.explanation: The forward reaction happens at the hot bottom. The gases move to the cool top, where the lower temperature causes the reverse reaction, reforming ammonium chloride.
acceptedAnswers: gases rise to the cooler part

questions.question:
Hydrogen and iodine react: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)
Write the equation for the reverse reaction and name the reactant in the reverse reaction.
markScheme: 1 mark: 2HI → H₂ + I₂
1 mark: hydrogen iodide
questions.explanation: The reverse reaction runs right to left, so hydrogen iodide is the reactant and hydrogen and iodine are the products.

questions.question: Write a balanced symbol equation, including state symbols, for the reversible decomposition of ammonium chloride. Explain what happens to the products when they are cooled.
markScheme: 1 mark: NH₄Cl ⇌ NH₃ + HCl with ⇌
1 mark: state symbols (s), (g), (g)
1 mark: on cooling ammonia and hydrogen chloride react to reform (white solid) ammonium chloride
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride is a solid, and ammonia and hydrogen chloride are gases. Cooling makes the reverse reaction happen.

questions.question:
Pink hydrated cobalt chloride turns blue when it is heated. When water is added to the blue solid, it turns pink again.
Explain how this shows that the reaction is reversible.
markScheme: 1 mark: heating produces anhydrous (blue) cobalt chloride and water (forward reaction)
1 mark: adding water makes the products react to reform the original (pink) hydrated cobalt chloride, so the reaction goes in both directions
questions.explanation: A reversible reaction is one where the products can react to form the original reactants. Here the products of heating (anhydrous cobalt chloride and water) recombine to give the starting substance.
acceptedAnswers: products react to reform the original reactant
blue anhydrous cobalt chloride and water reform pink hydrated cobalt chloride

questions.question: Describe how a student could show that the decomposition of ammonium chloride is a reversible reaction. Include what they would observe.
markScheme: Indicative content: place a small amount of ammonium chloride in the bottom of a test tube; clamp the tube at an angle (a loose plug of mineral wool can be placed in the mouth); heat the bottom gently with a Bunsen burner; work in a fume cupboard or well-ventilated room because ammonia and hydrogen chloride are toxic or irritant; wear eye protection; observe the white solid at the bottom getting smaller; observe a white solid forming on the cooler upper part of the tube; this shows ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride, with heating causing the forward reaction and cooling causing the reverse reaction.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): a clear, logical method with observations at both ends of the tube, linked to forward and reverse reactions.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, for example 'heat it and a white solid forms', with little explanation.
questions.explanation: A good answer gives a workable method, the observations, and links them to the reversible reaction. Safety points show the method is sensible.

questions.question:
A student writes: 'All chemical reactions can be reversed easily by changing the temperature.'
Evaluate this statement. Use examples in your answer.
markScheme: Indicative content: some reactions are reversible, for example ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride or hydrated copper sulfate ⇌ anhydrous copper sulfate + water; in these, heating and cooling change the direction; but many reactions are not easily reversed, for example combustion of methane or magnesium burning; the products of combustion (carbon dioxide, water, magnesium oxide) do not reform the reactants when cooled; so the statement is incorrect; only some reactions are reversible; even reversible reactions may appear to go one way in an open system if a gaseous product escapes.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): judgement that the statement is wrong, supported by at least one correct reversible example and one correct irreversible example with reasoning.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): a simple judgement with one example or limited reasoning.
questions.explanation: Evaluate means give evidence for and against, then reach a judgement. Only some reactions are reversible.

questions.question:
Ammonium chloride is a white solid. A student heats some ammonium chloride in a test tube and also heats some in an open evaporating basin.
Explain the observations in each case. Use ideas about reversible reactions and include an equation.
markScheme: Indicative content: equation ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride or NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + HCl(g); on heating, the forward reaction happens: ammonium chloride decomposes into two colourless gases; in the test tube the white solid at the bottom disappears; the gases rise to the cooler top of the tube; at the lower temperature the reverse reaction happens and white ammonium chloride forms on the glass; in the open basin the solid also disappears; the gases escape into the air and spread out; they cannot react back together so little or no white solid reforms in the basin; the reaction is still reversible, but the products are lost; the direction of the reaction depends on conditions (temperature); mass is conserved, but the mass in the open basin decreases because gases escape.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): a detailed and coherent explanation of both set-ups, using forward and reverse reactions linked to temperature, explaining why the open basin differs, with a correct equation.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains the test tube observations using the reversible reaction and makes some comparison with the basin, possibly with a correct word equation.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements about the solid disappearing or reforming, with little explanation.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that the same reversible reaction happens in both cases, but only in the test tube can the gases reach a cool region and react back before escaping.
